fixer.title: chat: Share and rate-limit core utility model requests

introducer.title: tool calls in dropdown and thinking headers

cases.mechanism: Each finalized uncached thinking block immediately started its own language-model request, so restoring a session with B blocks created B concurrent extension-host/network requests with no aggregate limiter or cross-render coalescing.
cases.symptom: Long-session restoration could burst utility-model traffic and receive HTTP rate limits; the PR metadata reports 429 telemetry, while the changed call path and new concurrency test directly establish the prior unbounded fan-out.
cases.fixedBehavior: Thinking-title requests now enter one shared limiter capped at three active background requests, share an in-flight request by cache key, and drop queued requests after all callers cancel.
cases.evidence: The deleted base call at the blamed line directly invoked `sendChatRequest` from every block's title finalization. The added caller marks title requests `background: true` with a stable key, line 82 queues them in the service's three-wide limiter, and the added test asserts only three background requests run concurrently while duplicate `b1` callers produce one send.
